specific_concerns.1_pre_repo_check_order: CONFIRMED by direct trace of do_get_instance_state/3 in platform.ex. Control flow: (a) prefix == nil clause -> "no_execution_context", returns before touching args at all; (b) [raw_id | _rest] when is_binary(raw_id) -> Ecto.UUID.cast(raw_id); on :error -> "invalid_id", still no Repo reference anywhere in this branch; (c) on {:ok, instance_id} -> `if instance_id == execution_context.instance_id do fetch_instance_state(...) else encode_error(lua, "forbidden") end`. fetch_instance_state/3 -- the only function in this module that references Repo -- is called from exactly one call site, gated behind that equality check. A mismatch takes the `else` branch and returns straight from do_get_instance_state/3; Repo.get/3 is never invoked, never referenced, on that path. Confirmed by reading the literal source, not the self-report.
specific_concerns.2_forbidden_indistinguishability: CONFIRMED, both on shape and on the mechanism that would produce a timing signal. Shape: both the sibling-instance case and the nonexistent-id case take the identical `else -> encode_error(lua, "forbidden")` branch inside do_get_instance_state/3 -- there is no separate code path that first checks existence for one case and not the other; encode_error/2 is a single shared function called with the same literal string in both cases, producing byte-identical {[nil], %{reason: "forbidden"}} shapes. Timing: since the mismatch check happens on the script-supplied UUID compared to execution_context.instance_id (a value already held in memory from the closure, no I/O), and fetch_instance_state/3 (the only path with a DB round-trip) is provably unreached in the mismatch branch, there is no differential DB round-trip between the sibling and nonexistent case -- both complete in the same number of Repo calls (zero). The remaining Ecto.UUID.cast/1 call executes identically for any syntactically valid UUID regardless of whether it corresponds to a real row, so no observable timing difference is introduced by this code. The test suite's own 'real same-tenant sibling instance AND a nonexistent instance id both return the IDENTICAL forbidden result' case (platform_test.exs) exercises exactly this and asserts value-level equality, which is consistent with the code trace. Confirmed sufficient given the actual code path (no Repo call in either branch); this is a stronger property than INV-5 formally requires today.
specific_concerns.3_repo_prefix_provenance: CONFIRMED. fetch_instance_state(instance_id, prefix, lua) is called from exactly one call site: `fetch_instance_state(instance_id, execution_context.prefix, lua)`, only inside the `if instance_id == execution_context.instance_id do` branch. Repo.get(InstanceProjection, instance_id, prefix: prefix) inside fetch_instance_state/3 binds `prefix` to that same parameter -- traced back, it is always execution_context.prefix, a value from the closure captured once per install/3 call, never from `raw_id`/the Lua call's argument list, directly or via any intermediate transform. grep confirms exactly one Repo.get( occurrence in the file, matching the structural test guard already present in platform_test.exs.
specific_concerns.4_read_variable_no_repo: CONFIRMED. do_read_variable/3's two clauses are pure Map.fetch/2 lookups against the `variables` field destructured directly from the execution_context argument (closed-over, itself not Lua-visible), plus a Lua.encode!/2 call to marshal the result back into a Lua table where needed. Neither clause, nor run_stub(:read_variable, ...), nor any function read_variable's path calls into references any Repo or Ecto.Repo alias.
specific_concerns.5_log_correlation_source: CONFIRMED. do_log/3 builds its metadata keyword list with `script_identity: execution_context.script_identity, instance_id: execution_context.instance_id, trace_id: execution_context.trace_id` -- all three read exclusively off the execution_context parameter. split_log_args/1 extracts only {level, message, context} from the Lua call's args list; there is no code path in do_log/3, split_log_args/1, or run_stub(:log, ...) that reads a 4th/5th script argument or any script-supplied key into those three metadata fields, optionally or otherwise.
specific_concerns.6_flagged_deviations_security_neutral: CONFIRMED for both. (a) run_stub/4 -> run_stub/5: this only changes how the already-decided values (row.stub, row.name, args, execution_context, plus the call's own Lua.t()) are threaded to reach Lua.encode!/2 for building a return table -- it does not add, remove, or reorder any capability check or context-derivation step; Capabilities.check!/3 still runs, in install/3's wrapper, strictly before run_stub/5 is ever invoked, unchanged from install/2's prior structure. (b) log's Lua.decode!/2 on `context`: decode_log_context/2 converts a raw {:tref,id} table reference into a decoded proplist purely for logging fidelity -- it does not touch script_identity/instance_id/trace_id (those never pass through decode at all, sourced only from execution_context per concern 5), and does not introduce any new Repo access or capability bypass. Both are implementation-mechanics fixes forced by the real tv-labs/lua API surface, not shortcuts around any security property.
specific_concerns.7_execution_context_non_influenceable: CONFIRMED. execution_context is a plain Elixir map parameter to install/3, constructed by the caller of install/3 (today: only test code and empty_execution_context/0's sentinel via install/1 -> install/2 -> install/3); it is captured once via closure inside install/3's Enum.reduce/3 fold and is never itself installed as a Lua global, never read from any Lua table, and no `args` value from any Lua call is ever merged into it. install/1's and install/2's delegation to empty_execution_context/0 (%{instance_id: nil, prefix: nil, trace_id: nil, script_identity: nil, variables: %{}}) is a fixed, hardcoded sentinel with no script-influenceable field. Sandbox.new/1's existing call site (lib/letflow/engine/lua/sandbox.ex:273, `Letflow.Engine.Lua.Platform.install()`) still invokes the arity-1 form unchanged, so every production VM today runs with the empty sentinel until a future requirement wires a real execution_context through Sandbox.new/1 or Executor -- this is explicitly out of REQ-159's owned_modules per the design's OQ-1, and does not weaken any property verified above since no script content can reach install/3's execution_context argument regardless of who calls it.

result.notes: get_instance_state (concerns 1-3) and log/read_variable (concerns 4-5) were traced directly against the committed source in commit e153fd5, not against ELIXIR-DEV's self-report or the design doc's prose. The security-critical self-instance-scoping fix required at design review (Step 1b) is correctly and completely realized in the implementation: the instance_id equality check occurs strictly before any Repo reference, and the forbidden result is structurally identical (same branch, same function call, zero DB round-trips) for a real sibling instance and a nonexistent id.
